source: Actual isolated authenticated PostgreSQL wheel probe with half-value prizes and minimum bonus payouts; every public/auth row rolled back. Legacy v3 diamond receipt retained from preceding qualified fixture. Seeds are synthetic test-only.
recalibration: Re-read on 2026-09-20 under the one-board, ten-drop rule. Sealed values are untouched: every server_seed, server_seed_hash, client_seed, nonce, commit_id, award and funding block is as captured. The Plinko batch is the FIRST TEN drops the same recorded seed produces, re-derived with the server algorithm hmac(server_seed, client_seed:nonce:drop:index) for the path and hmac(server_seed, client_seed:nonce:rounding:index) for the unbiased cent rounding; both were verified to reproduce every captured drop and every fractional-cent rounding in this file before it was rewritten. The board is the one the stake kind owns (fn_plinko_table_version: 5 Diamond, 4 Super) and payout_version follows it (1 ordinary, 3 Super). The quote block on a pending award is fn_diamond_bonus_minimum, fn_plinko_table_version and fn_choice_mode applied to the captured award. Settled rounds on the retired ladders keep their recorded mode, because the contract still reads them. The crossing and mines award quote is the one setting too: its prizes and max_steps are fn_choice_prizes(game, fn_choice_mode(game), bet_chips, award boost) - the twelve road streets, or six mines in twenty-five tiles over the award floor - cut by fn_wheel_bonus_state's own cap loop, which reproduced every captured ladder on the retired settings before these were recomputed. The Plinko board list in a quote is the two tables the migration leaves open, Super (4) and Diamond (5), with fn_plinko_table_audit's sd_chips and fn_wheel_bonus_state's availability against the award cap; Steady, Bold and Moonshot are closed and no longer quoted.
